extracted text: The paper focuses on AA2219 aluminum alloy in the T87 condition. This is an Al-Cu alloy used in aerospace applications. The paper mentions that the bulk of AA2219's strength comes from metastable θ' precipitates that form during aging. The study evaluates different processing conditions: without solution treatment (WST-CR), with solution treatment (ST+CR), and solution treated, cryorolled, and annealed (CR+Annealed). Solution treatment was performed at 808K (535°C) for 1 hour followed by water quenching. Annealing was done at 623K (350°C) for 1 hour. Cryorolling was achieved by dipping bars in liquid nitrogen for 30 minutes before the first pass and 15 minutes between passes. Cross-sectional area reduction achieved per pass was about 10%.

T87 = Temper designation indicating solution heat treated, artificially aged, and cold worked
WST = Without Solution Treatment
CR = Cryorolled
ST = Solution Treated
ANN/Annealed = Annealed
pct = percent
BHN = Brinell Hardness Number
IACS = International Annealed Copper Standard
